Test Description: Sanity check of USB memory-mapped register access: read from 0xA0000000 and 0xA001706C, write 0xDEADBEEF to 0xA0240000, read back the same location, and log the results before exiting.
Meta Test Description: The test_case() function performs basic MMIO operations using read_reg/write_reg on USB addresses. Sequence: initialize rd_data=0; rd_data=read_reg(0xA0000000); print value; rd_data=read_reg(0xa001706c); print value; write_reg(0xA0240000,0xdeadbeef); rd_data=read_reg(0xA0240000); print value; finish(0).
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Initialize the USB MMIO read/write test and logging.
2) Read and log the value from USB MMIO address 0xA0000000.
3) Read and log the value from USB MMIO address 0xA001706C.
4) Write the test pattern 0xDEADBEEF to USB MMIO address 0xA0240000.
5) Read and log back the value from USB MMIO address 0xA0240000 after the write.
6) Conclude the test run and report completion.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Declare int rd_data=0.
2) Call rd_data = read_reg(0xA0000000); then printf("THE READ DATA is %X\n", rd_data).
3) Call rd_data = read_reg(0xa001706c); then printf("THE READ DATA1 is %X\n", rd_data).
4) Call write_reg(0xA0240000, 0xdeadbeef).
5) Call rd_data = read_reg(0xA0240000); then printf("THE READ DATA2 is %X\n", rd_data).
6) Call finish(0).
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Test passes if the MMIO reads from 0xA0000000 and 0xA001706C execute without faults, the write to 0xA0240000 followed by read completes without error, the logged outputs show hexadecimal values for all three reads, and the test terminates cleanly (finish with status 0).
Meta Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- No exceptions or faults during read_reg/write_reg operations.
- Console prints present for three reads: "THE READ DATA is %X", "THE READ DATA1 is %X", and "THE READ DATA2 is %X" with some hex values.
- finish(0) is executed indicating normal completion.

Test Description: Configure the USB xHCI host controller, set up event/command infrastructure, enable interrupts, reset and initialize the host port, then perform EP0 control transfers (GET/SET configuration and descriptors) to enumerate a low-speed device. Validate using interrupt-driven event completions and port status.
Meta Test Description: The test_case() programs the xHCI controller registers and memory structures to perform host-side LS device enumeration. Sequence: initialize NIC and enable GIC interrupts; program GCTL, fladj_30mhz_reg, GUCTL; set PIPE/PHY control at BASE+0xC2C0/BASE+0xC200; read HCSPARAMS1, SUPTPRT2_DW2, SUPTPRT3_DW2, and PORTSC_20; enable PORTSC_20 wake bits and write 0xE0002A0; read DBOFF; program Event_Ring_Segment_Table and Default_Event_Ring_Array (size), read HCSPARAMS2 and PAGESIZE; program Scratchpad_Buffer_Array (SCRATCHPAD0/1) and Device_Context_Base_Address_Array entries; set CRCR_LO/HI to Default_Command_Ring, CONFIG to 0x10 then 0x110; program DCBAAP_LO/HI; set ERSTSZ=1, ERDP_LO/HI to Default_Event_Ring_Array, ERSTBA_LO/HI; clear IMOD, enable IMAN, enable USBCMD interrupt and run/stop=1; enable system INTR_EN0. Wait for interrupts (int_pend cleared by Default_IRQHandler), acknowledge USBSTS, re-enable IMAN, and read PORTSC_20. Advance ERDP, issue port reset via PORTSC_20 writes (0xE0006F1 then 0xE220200), wait for interrupt. Issue Enable Slot command TRB in Default_Command_Ring; service events (USBSTS/IMAN/ERDP), write PORTSC_20 (0xE200E01), ring DB, wait for interrupt. Build Default_Input_Context (slot/EP0 contexts and EP0_TR_Dequeue_Pointer) and issue Address Device commands (two phases) via Default_Command_Ring, servicing events and updating ERDP; wait for interrupt and read event completion. Call enumeration(): program EP0 TRBs for GET_DESCRIPTOR(Device), GET_CONFIGURATION, SET_CONFIGURATION, and additional GET_CONFIGURATIONs (with DATA and status TRBs), ring doorbell (BASE+0x484=0x1), then poll Default_Event_Ring_Array+0x110 until non-zero. Return to test_case and finish(0). Default_IRQHandler reads MSK_STS0 and RAW_STCR0, if RAW_STCR0 bit 31 set then masks IMAN and clears RAW_STCR0 bit, then clears GIC IRQ; it clears int_pend to release waits.
Remarks: Requires a low-speed USB device connected to the host port for enumeration. Test relies on interrupt handling to clear pending status and advance event processing. Event ring, device context base address array, scratchpad buffers, and EP0 transfer ring memory must be valid and accessible.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Initialize the platform and enable global USB interrupts in the GIC and system registers.
2) Configure the host controller basics: program GCTL, fladj_30mhz_reg, and GUCTL; apply PIPE and PHY control settings.
3) Read capability and port/PHY information (HCSPARAMS1/2, SUPTPRT2_DW2, SUPTPRT3_DW2, PAGESIZE) and check the port status.
4) Enable wake features on PORTSC_20 and apply initial port control settings; obtain doorbell offset (DBOFF).
5) Set up the Event Ring (Event_Ring_Segment_Table, Default_Event_Ring_Array) and pointers; program DCBAA and scratchpads; initialize the Command Ring (CRCR_LO/HI) and CONFIG.
6) Program ERST/ERDP/ERSTBA, enable IMAN/IMOD and USBCMD interrupt, enable system interrupt (INTR_EN0), then start the host (USBCMD run).
7) Wait for the first interrupt to confirm controller activity; acknowledge USBSTS and re-arm IMAN; verify the port is connected in PORTSC_20.
8) Advance ERDP and reset the port via PORTSC_20; wait for the corresponding interrupt and acknowledge.
9) Issue Enable Slot on the Command Ring; service events by acknowledging USBSTS, re-arming IMAN, advancing ERDP; set required PORTSC_20 state and ring the doorbell (DB) as needed; wait for completion interrupt.
10) Build the Input Context for Address Device (slot context and EP0 context with EP0 TR dequeue pointer) and issue Address Device commands; service events and update ERDP between phases until completion is reported.
11) Perform enumeration control transfers on EP0: GET device descriptor, GET configuration, SET configuration, and follow-up GET configuration requests; ring the controller doorbell to process TRBs.
12) Poll the Event Ring until a completion is observed for the final enumeration stage; declare pass when completions are received and the flow ends without errors.
